[P2] Account for the output device of factory-like random ops

This checks the input device, but `rand_like` and `randn_like` can generate on an explicitly different output device. With the CPU-local DTensor on a CUDA mesh constructed in the new test, `torch.rand_like(dt, device="cuda")` previously entered the CUDA tracker's `_distribute_region` and generated CUDA output with the appropriate RNG. This guard now rejects it solely because the input is on CPU.

Please check the effective generation device for these factory-like operators, accounting for an explicit `device` override, and add regression coverage for CPU input with CUDA output (`rand_like` and `randn_like`).

Verified by tracing the source; I have not run a runtime reproduction.

— Astra agent
